title: Nonzero differential detects generic etaleness for smooth curves
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X,Y$ be smooth curves over $k$, meaning separated integral schemes of finite type over $k$ of dimension one [def-pc-curve, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of a $k$-scheme $Z$, the sheaf $\Omega_{Z/k}$ is the sheaf associated with the module $\Omega_{B/k}$ of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. For every $k$-morphism $h:X\to Y$, the induced morphism of sheaves $dh:h^*\Omega_{Y/k}\to\Omega_{X/k}$, defined on local functions by $da\mapsto d(h^\sharp a)$, is nonzero if and only if there is a nonempty open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ such that $h|_V:V\to Y$ is étale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Here $h^*$ is module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Every nonempty affine open of either integral curve has dimension one. Indeed [def-sc-function-field] identifies their fraction fields with the same generic stalk, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] gives the same dimension to all such affines; their supremum is the dimension one of the curve. Thus every nonempty open neighbourhood of a point has dimension one, and the structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are smooth of relative dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] with $d=1$ to $X$ and $Y$. Both differential sheaves are locally free of rank one. The tensor formula in [def-pc-module-pullback] shows that $h^*\Omega_{Y/k}$ is also locally free of rank one: pull back a local basis and its inverse coordinate map.

The morphism $h$ is locally of finite presentation. Around any source point choose affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $A=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_r)$ finitely presented over $k$, using smoothness and [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; the chart can be made small enough to map into the target affine by principal localization, which adjoins one variable and one relation. Choose $k$-algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ of $B$ and polynomial representatives $G_i(x)$ for their images in $A$. Then $$A\cong B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_r,b_1-G_1,\ldots,b_m-G_m).$$ Evaluation gives the map to $A$; the reverse map sends each $x_j$ to its class. The finite relations of $A$ hold, and every element of $B$ is a polynomial in the $b_i$, so both composites fix all generators. This is a finite presentation for the original $B$-algebra map. In particular $h$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0C1C, verification of the finite-presentation hypothesis in 02G5 and 02GV

proof.text: On the affine charts of Step 2 apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-first-exact-sequence] to $k\to B\to A$. The first map sends $a\otimes db$ to $a\,d(h^\sharp b)$. Restricted to $\operatorname{Spec}A$, the pullback $h^*\Omega_{Y/k}$ is the pullback along $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ of the restriction of $\Omega_{Y/k}$, because inverse image and tensor product in [def-pc-module-pullback] are computed locally; [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] identifies it with the sheaf associated with $A\otimes_B\Omega_{B/k}$, the pulled-back section $db$ going to $1\otimes db$. So this first map is exactly $dh$ in the question. [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identifies the differential modules on principal restrictions, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] preserves the exact sequence on the stalk localizations. Consequently the affine sequences give the sheaf exact sequence $$h^*\Omega_{Y/k}\xrightarrow{dh}\Omega_{X/k}\longrightarrow\Omega_{X/Y}\longrightarrow0,$$ where the last sheaf has the affine meaning in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. Equivalently its stalk is the cokernel of the indicated differential map; this follows directly by localizing the affine sequence at each point.

Assume $dh\ne0$. Trivialize both rank-one sheaves on affine neighbourhoods. The map there is multiplication by a regular function $a$ in a domain. If its generic stalk were zero then $a$ would be zero in the fraction field, hence zero on each such affine, forcing $dh=0$. Thus on some nonempty affine chart $a\ne0$. Its principal open $D(a)$ is nonempty (it contains the generic point) and multiplication by $a$ is invertible there. Denote this open by $V$. By Step 3, $\Omega_{V/Y}=0$. Together with local finite type from Step 2, the affine differential characterization explicitly included in [def-weil-unramified-morphism] shows that $h|_V$ is unramified: the affine rings have zero relative differentials and are finitely generated over the target rings.

The map $h|_V$ is nonconstant. Suppose its image were the single point $y$. Every point of $V$ is a specialization of its generic point, so $y$ is the image of that point as well. If $y$ is the generic point of $Y$, the local homomorphism at a point $v$ corresponding to a maximal ideal in any nonempty affine chart of $V$ would embed $k(Y)$ into $\kappa(v)$. This is impossible: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-domain-dimension-trdeg] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k k(Y)=1$ and dimension one for $\mathcal O_{V,v}$, whereas [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(v)=0$. If $y$ is not generic, it is closed: in a dimension-one integral scheme every nongeneric point is closed, since an intermediate specialization would give a prime chain of length two. On an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $y$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, take a nonempty affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset V$. Every prime of $A$ contains the image of $\mathfrak m$; since $A$ is a domain this image is zero. Thus the original map factors through the field $K=B/\mathfrak m=\kappa(y)$. Derivations of $A$ over $B$ and over $K$ are identical because $B\to K$ is surjective, so $\Omega_{A/K}=\Omega_{A/B}=0$. The $k$-generators of $A$ also generate it over $K$, hence $W\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is unramified by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product]: $A$ is a finite product of fields and, as a domain, is a field. Its spectrum has dimension zero, contradicting Step 1. Both possible singleton images are excluded.

By [lem-sc-smooth-normal], the smooth curve $Y$ is normal. The nonempty open $V$ is again an integral separated finite-type dimension-one curve. Apply [lem-a1-nonconstant-normal-curve-map-flat] to $h|_V$, using Step 5 to supply its nonconstant hypothesis: this restriction is flat. It is locally of finite presentation by Step 2 and unramified by Step 4. Therefore it is etale by the precise flat, unramified, locally-finite-presentation definition in [def-weil-etale-morphism]. This proves the forward implication.

Conversely, suppose $h|_V$ is etale on a nonempty open $V\subset X$. It is unramified by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and its affine differential modules vanish by [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Step 3 restricted to $V$ therefore makes $dh|_V$ surjective onto $\Omega_{V/k}$. At any point of $V$ the latter stalk is a free module of rank one over a nonzero local ring, by Step 1. A zero map cannot surject onto it (its basis element $1$ is nonzero). Thus $dh|_V\ne0$, and consequently $dh\ne0$ on $X$. No finiteness of $h$, properness, perfectness of $k$, or rationality of a point was used.
